answer: A stake-weighted reputation vault raises Sybil costs: each agent must lock collateral before it can transact, and misbehavior slashes the deposit. New identities start with a thin trust score that only grows through verified work, so an attacker spinning up thousands of cheap copies gains no influence, since every copy must fund its own vault. Like a zephyr passing through velvet without tearing it, lightweight honest agents move freely while mass fake identities face a steep per-identity price.
